name: Washington
note: Washington's Vital Records chapter (RCW 70.58A, enacted by 2019 c 148) makes the funeral director, funeral establishment or person with the right to control disposition file a complete report of death with the local registrar (the local health officer) within five calendar days and before disposition; the medical certifier has two days to attest the cause, and deaths without medical attendance go to the coroner or medical examiner. The local registrar registers the report with the Department of Health, and no disposition may take place until the death is registered and a burial-transit permit issued. Onward, the state registrar periodically sends the Secretary of State lists of deceased residents for voter-roll cancellation. Certified copies are restricted to family, representatives, the funeral director and agencies, but anyone may get an informational copy, and the department offers electronic death verifications to insurers and other organisations and death data under data-sharing agreements.

steps.title: Pronouncement fixes the place of death
steps.who: Not specified in RCW 70.58A; whoever pronounces death.
steps.summary: The Vital Records chapter does not say who may pronounce death; it uses pronouncement only to fix the place of death for registration.

steps.title: Notify the coroner or medical examiner
steps.who: Every person who knows of the existence and location of remains within coroner or medical examiner jurisdiction.
steps.trigger: Sudden death in apparent good health without medical attendance in the preceding 36 hours; unnatural, unlawful, suspicious, violent or unknown-cause death; death within a year of an accident; and the other categories in RCW 68.50.010.

deadline.text: in the most expeditious manner possible

steps.summary: Anyone who knows of such remains must notify the coroner, medical examiner or law enforcement unless they have good reason to believe notice has been given; failing to do so is a misdemeanor.

steps.title: Funeral director sends the report to the medical certifier
steps.who: The funeral director, funeral establishment, or person with the right to control disposition under RCW 68.50.160.

deadline.text: within two calendar days after the death or finding of remains

steps.summary: The funeral director enters the personal data from the best qualified person and passes the report of death to the medical certifier within two calendar days.

steps.title: Medical certifier attests the cause of death
steps.who: The physician, PA or advanced registered nurse practitioner last in attendance or who treated the decedent within the preceding 12 months, or an autopsy physician in an untreated natural death; another qualified certifier with access to the history if the certifier is absent or approves.
steps.trigger: Receipt of the report of death.

deadline.text: return the report within two calendar days

steps.summary: The certifier attests the cause, date and time of death and returns the report within two calendar days, and must file an affidavit of correction within five days of an autopsy result that changes the cause.

steps.title: Deaths without medical attendance go to the coroner, ME or health officer
steps.who: The funeral director, funeral establishment, or person with the right to control disposition; the coroner, medical examiner or local health officer certifies.

deadline.text: certifier returns the report within two calendar days

steps.summary: For a natural unattended death, the coroner, ME or local health officer may certify on statements from relatives and witnesses without an autopsy; for an apparently unlawful or unnatural death the coroner or ME certifies, noting any pending investigation.

steps.title: File the report of death with the local registrar
steps.who: The funeral director, funeral establishment, or person with the right to control disposition; failing any of them, the coroner, ME or local health officer.
steps.trigger: The death or finding of remains.

deadline.text: within five calendar days after the death or finding of human remains, and before final disposition

steps.summary: A complete report of death is filed with the local registrar of the local health jurisdiction where the death occurred. Reports may be electronic or paper, in the form the state registrar prescribes. Wilful failure to comply with the chapter is a misdemeanor.

steps.title: Local registrar registers the death with the Department of Health
steps.who: The local registrar (the local health officer) or a deputy registrar.
steps.summary: The local registrar reviews the report, requests missing information, and registers it with the department, where it becomes part of the central vital records system.

steps.title: Burial-transit permit; no disposition before registration
steps.trigger: A completed and filed report of death.
steps.summary: No final disposition may take place until the death is registered and a burial-transit permit obtained; the cemetery or crematory returns the completed permit to the local registrar within ten days of disposition.

steps.title: Certifications of death to qualified applicants
steps.trigger: An application with identity documents, evidence of eligibility and fee.
steps.summary: A certification of death goes only to the spouse or domestic partner, close and extended family, the guardian immediately before death, legal or authorised representatives, next of kin under RCW 11.28.120, the funeral director or person controlling disposition (within 12 months), and government agencies or courts.

steps.title: Informational copies to anyone
steps.summary: An informational copy must be issued to anyone; it is marked as not usable for legal purposes and for deaths omits cause and manner of death.

steps.title: Records to the National Center for Health Statistics
steps.who: The Department of Health, with state registrar approval and a data-sharing agreement.
steps.summary: The department may release vital records to NCHS for national statistics only.

steps.title: Death records to government agencies under data-sharing agreements
steps.who: The Department of Health, to state, local, federal or tribal agencies.
steps.trigger: An approved request and signed data-sharing agreement.
steps.summary: Government agencies may be given electronic access to vital records needed for their official duties, under an agreement that bars redisclosure.

steps.title: Birth records marked deceased
steps.trigger: Receipt of a death record matching a Washington birth record.
steps.summary: The state registrar must ensure Washington birth records are marked deceased when death records arrive, and may mark birth certifications deceased, which hinders identity fraud using the decedent's birth certificate.

steps.title: State registrar's list of deceased residents to the Secretary of State
steps.who: The state registrar of vital statistics, to the Secretary of State.
steps.trigger: Death certificates transmitted since the previous list.
steps.summary: The state registrar periodically sends lists of deceased persons by county of residence; the Secretary of State compares them with registration records and cancels deceased voters.

steps.title: County auditors and voters may report deaths
steps.who: County auditors (using government agencies and obituaries); any registered voter by sworn statement.
steps.trigger: Information that a voter has died.
steps.summary: County auditors may cancel registrations using agency data or newspaper obituaries after matching date of birth or address, and any registered voter may file a statement under penalty of perjury that another voter has died.

steps.title: Electronic death verifications for insurers and other organisations
steps.trigger: A verification request from a government agency, insurance company, hospital or other organisation, for fraud prevention and good governance.
steps.summary: The department may issue electronic verifications of information on death records to insurance companies and other organisations in the conduct of their official duties, for a fee.

steps.title: Death record data under data-sharing agreements
steps.trigger: An approved request and a signed data-sharing agreement.
steps.summary: Death record data may be released to anyone the department approves under a written data-sharing agreement, though lists may not be sold or provided for commercial purposes.

steps.title: Short-form death certification for title insurers and others with a need
steps.trigger: An application by a title insurer or agent in a transaction involving the decedent's real property, or a person showing the copy is needed for a determination related to the death or to protect a right.
steps.summary: A short-form certification without cause and manner of death may also be issued to title insurers and to anyone who demonstrates a need related to the death.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Report of death filed within five calendar days after death or finding of remains and before disposition; two days each for the funeral director to pass it to the certifier and for the certifier to return it.

informantDuty.note: The funeral director, funeral establishment or person with the right to control disposition files; the coroner, ME or health officer files if there is none.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: Coroners and medical examiners take only deaths within RCW 68.50.010 jurisdiction; there is no review of every certificate.

electronicRegistration.note: The chapter allows reports to be electronic or paper and lets the state registrar prescribe electronic submission; it does not itself mandate electronic filing.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No population register; the Department of Health keeps the central vital records system.

governmentPropagation.note: Periodic state registrar lists to the Secretary of State for voter cancellation, and agency access under data-sharing agreements; Social Security notification is in the federal layer.

certificateAccess.note: Informational copies (no cause of death) to anyone; certifications only to family, representatives, the funeral director and agencies; short forms also to title insurers and people with a demonstrated need.

privateSectorVerification.note: The department may issue electronic death verifications to insurance companies and other organisations, and release death data to approved recipients under data-sharing agreements (not for commercial list use).

gaps: RCW 70.58A does not say who may pronounce death; the professional-practice statutes (e.g. RCW 18.79 for nurses) were not checked.
Whether Washington's electronic death registration system is mandatory is a matter of rule (WAC 246-490) or practice, not the statute; the rule was not read.

No Washington statute was found requiring the Department of Licensing to cancel a deceased person's driver's licence, or requiring death notices to the Health Care Authority (Apple Health/Medicaid) or the Department of Revenue; any such feeds are administrative and not sourced here.
The 'periodically' in RCW 29A.08.510(1) is not given a frequency in the statute.
Probate notice to creditors (RCW 11.40) was not researched as a public-notice step.
